our_profile.name: atf-graphrag Capability Profile
our_profile.summary: atf-graphrag is a comprehensive enterprise GraphRAG platform for ATF domain documents (firearms, explosives, manufacturing, trafficking). It features multi-modal ingestion with structure-aware parsing, typed knowledge graph construction, sophisticated multi-lane retrieval (vector/BM25/graph/SQL/table-row lookup), agentic quality gates at every pipeline stage, and AWS-native control plane integration. Ingestion routes documents (PDF/web/image) through specialized handlers with OCR/vision, outputs fine-grained metadata-rich chunks with table extraction and entity typing, and builds a queryable typed entity graph with resolution and community detection. Retrieval orchestrates six subagents (query understanding, corpus selection, hybrid retrieval with BFS/PPR graph modes, evaluation, reranking, generation) plus adaptive lanes (corrective retry, multi-hop decomposition, SQL over table store, deterministic row lookup, web research augmentation). All components are swappable via configuration (local/bedrock/openrouter profiles) and protected by quality gates (parse QA, chunk gate, metadata audit, index audit, graph quality, grounding verification).

techniques.technique: Structure-aware hierarchical chunking with content-type detection
techniques.what: Chunker classifies blocks as text/table/chart/figure/list via heuristics (markdown patterns, numeric field density, bullet detection). Tables are kept whole/atomic by row groups; charts/figures preserve their full description; lists are kept unbroken; prose uses sliding-window with sentence-boundary snapping. Each chunk carries content_type tag for downstream routing.
techniques.value: Prevents tables being fragmented across chunks (enabling whole-table retrieval), preserves chart context untruncated, protects list cohesion — all essential for multi-modal tables-and-graphs documents.

techniques.technique: Per-chunk table_data extraction with cell-level addressability
techniques.what: For chunks marked content_type='table', a structured dict {columns: [...], rows: [[...], ...]} captures the parsed cell grid. Built during chunking for markdown/columnar tables and by parsers (Docling, Textract, BDA) for PDF tables. Enables SQL queries and exact-match row lookup.
techniques.value: Solves the 'find row X in table Y' problem deterministically: embeddings/BM25 can't find one row among thousands; exact token matching in table_data makes it certain.

techniques.technique: Docling-based layout-aware PDF parsing with vision fallback
techniques.what: Default parser is Docling (DocLayNet layout models + TableFormer table structure). Returns (page_no, text) tuples with tables as markdown and pictures (≥80px) sent to VLM for [VLM CHART (p2_img3)] descriptions. Gracefully degrades to AdvancedParser (PyMuPDF+pdfplumber) if Docling unavailable or PDF fails, preserving VLM cache and scanned-page fallback.
techniques.value: Docling extracts borderless/complex tables and respects layout flow order (top→bottom, left→right); fallback keeps system runnable without heavy ML deps. VLM pictures prevent decorative logos from diluting text content.

techniques.technique: Multi-provider parser ecosystem with automatic fallback
techniques.what: Config selects parser: docling (Docling), advanced (PyMuPDF+pdfplumber), textract (AWS Textract), bedrock (AWS foundation models), or bda (Amazon Bedrock Data Automation). Each degrades to the next if dependency missing or call fails. Same contract: (page_no, text) tuples with tables as markdown.
techniques.value: Lets users choose speed (advanced) vs quality (Docling) vs AWS-native (Textract, Bedrock, BDA) without touching code; offline fallback ensures no stuck deployments.

techniques.technique: Heuristic + LLM-based entity extraction with typed ontology
techniques.what: Heuristic pass: regex-extracts dates, years, states, case refs, proper-noun entities, sellers/buyers, firearm/incident types (domain vocab lists). LLM enrichment (when configured): ontology-constrained extraction yields 7 entity types + 8 relation types with descriptions; parsed entities populate typed ChunkRecord fields (manufacturers, firearm_type, location, etc.) and rec._entity_meta (transient, not persisted).
techniques.value: Offline-first extraction guarantees graph works without keys; LLM adds typed relations (descriptions) for richer graph semantics and node verification.

techniques.technique: Agentic orchestrator with routing classification and idempotency manifest
techniques.what: classify() probes inputs (PDF page sparseness/images), returns RouteDecision (input_type, corpus, ocr/vision/tables flags, extract_entities, use_graph logic). Routes to handlers: file, batch, image, website, sitemap. Idempotency manifest maps corpus:doc_id→{hash, chunks}; skip unchanged docs, delete-then-reindex changed ones.
techniques.value: Different source types need different logic; probing avoids sending scanned PDFs to text-only parser. Manifest prevents re-processing and duplicate indexing when corpus is re-run.

techniques.technique: Parallel typed-graph enrichment with journaled resumability
techniques.what: GraphEnricher runs pool of extraction workers over pending chunks (prose, ≥300 chars, ≥45% alpha). Parallel LLM extraction populates relationships + entity metadata; graph writes serialized under lock. Processed chunk IDs journaled to enrich_journal.json so stopped jobs resume from last write.
techniques.value: Typed edges (evidence-backed) separate from co-occurrence hairball so community detection and PPR see only real relations. Journaling makes hour-long enrichment jobs safe to interrupt.

techniques.technique: Leiden community detection with size constraints and LLM cluster summaries
techniques.what: Community builder converts LocalGraphStore to networkx (with Phase-A pruning applied), runs Leiden (graspologic) or fallback Louvain, filters clusters by min_community_size, builds per-cluster summary (LLM per cluster, cached by member hash). Returns communities.json with {entities, relations, chunk_ids, summary}.
techniques.value: Tight communities (max_cluster_size=10) cluster-to-summary cost is linear. Summaries are cached so re-ingesting unchanged clusters burns zero tokens. Communities power 'global' mode answering.

techniques.technique: QueryUnderstandingAgent with intent detection and LLM refinement
techniques.what: Heuristic: keyword bins (REL_WORDS, TIMELINE_WORDS, TABLE_WORDS, VISUAL_WORDS, etc., MANUFACTURE_WORDS, EXPORT_WORDS, ...) map question to intent (fact|entity|relationship|pattern|timeline|table|visual|multi) and set flags (use_graph, use_metadata). Optional LLM refinement calls the model to override (gated by llm_refine config, off in deterministic eval mode).
techniques.value: Intent routing ensures relationship questions hit graph retrieval, timeline questions apply metadata filters, table questions trigger SQL. Domain intent hints (manufacture, export, theft) feed domain-specific source boosts in retrieval.

techniques.technique: Hybrid retrieval with vector + BM25 + dynamic source diversity
techniques.what: Retrieval embeds question, searches each corpus with vector (top_k×3) and BM25 (top_k×2), merges by chunk_id keeping max score. Per-source cap _max_per_source dynamically scales (3 for ≤15 docs, 6 for ≥15) so diverse corpora don't get dominated by one large doc. Small-doc boost: docs <500 chunks get 1.5× multiplier.
techniques.value: BM25 catches keyword-dense rows/tables that embed poorly. Dynamic cap prevents one 10k-chunk AFMER doc drowning out 5-chunk specialized reports. Small-doc boost equalizes competition.

techniques.technique: Six-stage retrieval subagent pipeline with trace observability
techniques.what: 1) QueryUnderstandingAgent: intent+plan. 2) CorpusSelectionAgent: choose corpus(es). 3) RetrievalAgent: hybrid vector/BM25/graph/table-row. 4) EvaluationAgent: filter by relevance. 5) RerankingAgent: reorder by cross-encoder (local/LLM/bedrock). 6) GenerationAgent: call LLM. Each stage adds to trace dict; pipeline returns {trace, answer, citations}.
techniques.value: Six independent agents mean each can be tested, tuned, or swapped. Trace shows exactly where evidence came from (which agent, which corpus, which retrieval mode).

techniques.technique: Graph retrieval with BFS subgraph expansion and Personalized PageRank (PPR)
techniques.what: BFS (default): find query entities in graph, expand N hops, separate typed edges (0.65 score) from co-occurrence (0.5), return path labels. PPR (when graph_retriever='ppr' + relationship/pattern intent): seed personalization on query entities, rank chunks by pagerank, normalize into 0.50-0.70 band. Both use networkx with typed-edge weight boost (3×).
techniques.value: BFS returns all connected evidence at relationship distance. PPR ranks by centrality so 'hub' nodes (highly connected to seeds) rise to top — better for finding the core of a trafficking ring/pattern.

techniques.technique: Deterministic table-row exact-match lookup from structured table_data
techniques.what: extract_row_keys() pulls candidates from question: quoted strings, proper-noun runs ('EMCO INC'), license-like numbers. RowIndex inverts token→{chunk_ids} over table_data string cells. find_rows() intersects token sets, scans candidate chunks' rows for ones matching ALL tokens. Returns chunk + matched_row_text + year-boost score.
techniques.value: Eliminates embedding lottery for row lookup: if row exists with all named tokens, it will be found with score pinned into extraction_summary for generation to quote.

techniques.technique: Structured table store with SQL lane and category consolidation
techniques.what: TableStore.build() scans vector-store payloads for table_data, inserts into SQLite tables/rows with full provenance. find_tables() ranks candidate tables by token overlap + year match. query() calls LLM to generate SELECT (validated for SELECT-only, parses, executes, non-empty), returns result_rows with {tables, sql, rows, provenance}. consolidate() groups same-category tables (signature Jaccard ≥0.55) so cross-year questions see every edition.
techniques.value: SQL over exact cells avoids retrieval gambles. Cross-year category grouping lets 'compare 2025 vs 2026' pull both editions of a family automatically. Any failure falls back to RAG.

techniques.technique: Corrective retriever with query reformulation and retry loop
techniques.what: CorrectiveRetriever.improve() checks evidence sufficiency (top_eval_score < weak_top=0.45 OR <3 hits). If weak, reformulate question (LLM: synonyms/expansions; offline: content-token keyword expansion). Retrieve again with reformulated query, merge gained hits, re-evaluate vs ORIGINAL question. Max 1 retry (corrective_max_retries=1).
techniques.value: Weak evidence (top score 0.3, 2 hits) triggers reformulation and second pass. Deterministic offline reformulation ensures eval reproducibility. Single retry caps cost.

techniques.technique: Multi-hop query decomposition for bridge and comparison questions
techniques.what: MultiHopPlanner.decompose() uses LLM to split bridge/comparison questions into 2-3 sub-questions (e.g. 'Which dealer sold X?' → 'Find X', 'Find dealer selling X'). run() executes hops sequentially, each generating short intermediate answer, later hops substitute {hop1}/{hop2} refs. All hop evidence merged; hop chain shown to generator.
techniques.value: Comparison questions need BOTH sides retrieved; bridge questions need intermediate facts before finding the answer. Hop chain in trace shows the decomposition used.

techniques.technique: Generic comparison fan-out for 'A vs B' questions
techniques.what: is_comparison() detects compare/vs/versus/more...or keywords. comparison_targets() extracts compared entities: US states first (multi-word), then 4-digit years, then capitalized proper-noun phrases. Pipeline runs one retrieval per target, merges hits so BOTH A and B reach generation.
techniques.value: Ensures 'How many states exported more than California?' retrieves both California and all other states' data before asking the LLM the comparative question.

techniques.technique: Whole-table retrieval: sibling chunk collection for complete table rows
techniques.what: expand_whole_tables() builds lazy {(corpus, document_id, page): [chunk_id,...]} index over table chunks. After retrieval, for each table hit, adds its sibling table chunks from same page (up to 12 extra). Serves the 'all rows from table X' use case.
techniques.value: Retrieval returns table fragment (5 rows). Expansion grabs all 20 rows from the same page so generation sees the complete table, not a subset.

techniques.technique: Web research augmentation with novelty + source credibility tiers
techniques.what: WebResearchAgent.should_augment() decides: news-intent + thin evidence (top<0.45) or thin evidence alone triggers search. research() calls Tavily, per-result: relevance (keyword overlap OR provider_score×tier ≥0.55), novelty (embedding sim <0.88 vs corpus), LLM worthiness judge. Ingest ONLY worthy results (max 3/query). All logged in decision record.
techniques.value: Thin evidence on current events auto-triggers web search. Credibility tiers (.gov=1.0, blogspot=0.4) prevent random blog posts outweighting official releases. Novelty check avoids duplication.

techniques.technique: On-demand corpus selection with explicit pinning and heuristic routing
techniques.what: CorpusSelectionAgent.select() checks plan.filters['corpus'] first (explicit pinning). Falls back to heuristic: corpus name mentioned ('web corpus', 'visual data'), topic words (website→web, chart→visual). Returns intersection with available corpora.
techniques.value: API can pin a single corpus for isolated queries. Heuristics handle 'I want web results' without explicit pinning. Multi/fact questions use all available.

techniques.technique: Query-plan metadata filtering for date and location scoping
techniques.what: QueryUnderstandingAgent.plan() detects years/dates in question and sets use_metadata=True. RetrievalAgent._filter() builds where() callable: checks document_date + incident_date against query years, accepts chunk if year matches ANY query year OR chunk is undated. Applies hard filter at vector search level.
techniques.value: Questions like 'explosives incidents in 2024' filter to 2024 docs before ranking, avoiding 2022 docs even if they rank high. Undated docs always included (data completeness).

techniques.technique: Content-type boost and visual_boost for intent-driven scoring
techniques.what: Retrieval applies visual_boost=1.05 (configurable) when intent in (table, visual). Chunks with content_type in (table, chart, figure) get multiplied by boost factor (1.05 or 1.0). Chunk quality filter penalizes low-quality chunks (URLs, TOC lines, timestamps) down to 0.1-0.2 multiplier.
techniques.value: Visual questions see slight boost for visual content without over-boosting (avoids flooding with mislabeled chunks). Quality filter prevents garbage (navigation) from crowding data.

techniques.technique: Year-based scoring adjustments: match +30%, mismatch -20%, undated -15%
techniques.what: When question mentions year(s), RetrievalAgent boosts: year-matched docs (year in source_name OR document_date) +30%, dated docs with wrong year -20%, undated docs -15%. Applied after diversity capping to reorder surviving hits.
techniques.value: Ensures 2024 question prefers 2024 doc over 2022 doc even if 2022 is larger and has higher base BM25 score. Undated penalty prevents them from dominating (when they're truly wrong for the question).

techniques.technique: Domain-specific source boosts for manufacture/export/selling/theft/trace
techniques.what: plan.filters['domain'] set by keywords (MANUFACTURE_WORDS→'manufacture', EXPORT_WORDS→'export'). RetrievalAgent applies 1.8× boost to chunks from domain-matched sources (AFMER for manufacture, nfcta_export for export). Pre-fetch domain sources at top_k×2 to ensure boosts have candidates.
techniques.value: Export queries retrieve import data semantically (both are country×firearm tables); 1.8× source boost on nfcta_export overcomes small-doc disadvantage. AFMER queries prefer AFMER over generic commerce reports.

techniques.technique: Phase-A graph pruning: weak/untyped edges between obscure nodes
techniques.what: pruning.kept_edges() drops edges IFF (not typed) AND weight < min_edge_weight AND both endpoints degree < min_degree. Hub nodes (top-X% degree) optionally removed before clustering to split dense co-occurrence hairballs. Used by community detection and PPR.
techniques.value: Typed edges (evidence-backed) always kept. Prevents thousands of weight-1 co-occurrence edges fracturing clusters. PPR on pruned graph ranks truly central entities, not noise.

techniques.technique: Global/sensemaking mode with community-based map-reduce answering
techniques.what: QueryUnderstandingAgent.plan() routes 'across', 'overall', 'common themes', 'most frequent' questions to mode='global' when communities built. Retriever.answer() runs GlobalAnswerAgent: extracts topic clusters from question, maps each community summary for relevance, reduces by merging. Falls back to local lane if global answer is insufficient (<25 chars or refusal markers).
techniques.value: Sensemaking questions ('What are recurring patterns?') answered from community summaries (map-reduce) NOT individual chunks, capturing corpus-wide perspective. Fallback keeps specific-data questions working.

techniques.technique: Mixed-mode retrieval: local lane + community context fusion
techniques.what: Questions with specific intent (table) but global scope route to mode='mixed'. Runs full local retrieval + corpus-wide community context: top_k=3 relevant communities added to graph_paths (shown to generator as 'KNOWN RELATIONSHIP PATHS'). Generator sees both fine-grained evidence and high-level patterns.
techniques.value: Avoids false dichotomy of 'local detail' vs 'global pattern'. Mixed mode gives generator both.

techniques.technique: Reranking with local cross-feature + optional LLM/Bedrock cross-encoder
techniques.what: RerankingAgent.rerank() default: local cross-feature (question-to-chunk relevance via feature similarity). Optional LLM reranker (slower, uses model to score) or Bedrock reranker (Cohere Rerank model). Reordered hits returned with rerank_score.
techniques.value: Local reranking is instant (no model call). LLM reranking uses semantic understanding (slower, opt-in). Bedrock reranker offloads to managed service.

techniques.technique: Evaluation agent with relevance + consistency checks
techniques.what: EvaluationAgent filters hits by relevance (low scores dropped), consistency (checks for contradictions vs other hits), and completeness (flagged for 'incomplete' when answer is numeric but no table/chart). Returns filtered + flagged hits.
techniques.value: Prevents contradictory context confusing generation. Flags incomplete numeric answers so generator adds 'incomplete evidence' caveat.

techniques.technique: Six quality-gate subagents at pipeline boundaries
techniques.what: ParseQualityAgent: re-parse if empty_ratio>0.7 OR garble_ratio>0.02. ChunkGateAgent: block junk (short, URL-only, nav timestamps) unless table/vision/summary. MetadataAuditAgent: coverage report for CRITICAL + VALUABLE fields. IndexAuditAgent: round-trip probe (embed chunk, search, confirm doc surfaces). GraphQualityAgent: junk-node rate + typed-edge ratio. GroundingVerifierAgent: numbers in answer must appear in context; one strict regenerate if violations found.
techniques.value: Each gate is a deterministic rule-based check (no LLM except grounding verify). Gates catch bad parser output, junk chunks, metadata gaps, index bugs, graph pollution, hallucinated numbers BEFORE they reach the user.

techniques.technique: Storage durability: epoch guard + single-writer lock
techniques.what: epoch_guard.py: every restore/clear writes fresh UUID to /.epoch. Stores load their startup epoch; commit() re-reads file and raises StaleWriteError if epoch changed (stale writer trying to clobber newer data). storage_lock.py: /.writer.lock holds PID; second writer refuses to start.
techniques.value: Prevents data clobber from stale processes/threads holding old in-memory state. Epoch guards same-process stale references; lock guards inter-process concurrency.

techniques.technique: Config-driven component swapping: local | bedrock | hybrid profiles
techniques.what: config.py DEFAULTS: local (OpenRouter + local stores). Config + env overrides select providers: llm.provider=bedrock, embeddings.provider=bedrock, vector_store.provider=opensearch, etc. Engine factory makes each provider (graceful degradation on missing dep). Same code runs across all profiles.
techniques.value: No AWS code path needed for local dev. Swapping to Bedrock is a config change. Each provider defaults to local, so missing a dependency doesn't crash.

techniques.technique: Lazy provider loading and graceful fallback
techniques.what: Each make_<component>() factory tries the configured provider, catches exceptions, falls back to local with a one-line warning. e.g. make_parser('docling') → tries DoclingParser, on ImportError returns AdvancedParser. Components are lazy-loaded (DocumentConverter only created on first PDF).
techniques.value: Docling not installed? Uses PyMuPDF silently. AWS credentials missing? Runs local embedder. No stuck deployments or dependency hell.

external_profiles.name: PixelRAG (StarTrail-org)
external_profiles.summary: PixelRAG is a pixel-native (screenshot-based) RAG system from Berkeley SkyLab/BAIR/NLP. Instead of parsing documents to text, it renders web pages/PDFs/images to screenshot tiles, embeds each tile with a LoRA-fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B vision-language model, indexes vectors in FAISS, and at query time retrieves the most visually similar tiles and feeds the raw images to a VLM reader. The thesis: visual structure (tables, charts, layout) that HTML/text parsing destroys stays intact when retrieving over pixels.
external_profiles.ingestion: Standalone `pixelshot` CLI captures pages; the `pixelrag` umbrella runs a sequential render → chunk → embed → index pipeline. Rendering uses Playwright/Chrome CDP (headless Chromium) plus poppler for PDFs to produce screenshots of documents (web pages, PDFs, images) at a fixed render width. Output is image tiles, not text. A `pixelrag chunk` stage turns rendered captures into tile units; a `pixelrag embed` stage turns tiles → vectors; `pixelrag index` builds the FAISS index; `pixelrag serve` exposes a FastAPI search endpoint (CPU or GPU). Ships a prebuilt 8.28M-page Wikipedia index (~30M tiles per secondary reporting) and a hosted API at api.pixelrag.ai. NOTE: exact tile height/overlap/page-splitting params are not stated in the main README or train README — could not verify precise tiling geometry.
external_profiles.chunking: Visual tiling instead of text chunking. A long page is rendered at a fixed width and split into screenshot tiles (vertical segments) rather than token-bounded text chunks. The stated advantage over text RAG: tiling by visual region keeps a table or chart as a single intact retrievable unit, whereas token-limit chunking splits/loses tables. The README's worked example: text RAG "parses the page to text chunks and loses the table"; PixelRAG "renders the page to screenshot tiles, retrieves the right tile, and the reader reads the number straight off the image." Exact tile dimensions and overlap not documented in sources I could read.
external_profiles.retrieval: Single-vector dense retrieval (NOT ColPali-style multi-vector late-interaction — the train recipe uses a single embedding per tile via `train_contrastors.py`, an InfoNCE-style contrastive objective; no MaxSim/late-interaction was found). Query and tile are embedded into a shared VL space by the fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B; nearest-neighbor search runs over a FAISS index served by FastAPI. Supports image-as-query (visual search), not just text queries. No sparse/BM25 lane, no hybrid fusion, and no reranker are described in the docs I read. Retrieved tiles are passed directly to a downstream VLM reader (e.g. GPT-4o / Claude) which reads the answer off the pixels.
external_profiles.graph: No knowledge graph. There is no entity/relation extraction, no GraphRAG/LightRAG-style dual-level keys, and no graph traversal anywhere in the architecture. Retrieval is flat vector NN over tile embeddings. (Relevant caveat for a graph-based ATF RAG: PixelRAG offers nothing on the graph axis; its contributions are all on the multimodal-retrieval and training-data axes.)
external_profiles.multimodal: This is the whole point of the project. Tables, charts, layout, and infographics are preserved by never converting to text — they remain pixels inside the retrieved tile, and a VLM reader extracts the answer from the image at read time. Handles web pages, PDFs, and standalone images uniformly (all become screenshots). Equations are not called out explicitly but would be preserved as image content by the same mechanism. No separate table-structure parser, OCR, or chart-to-data extraction step exists — fidelity comes from keeping the rendered pixels and using a vision reader, which secondary reporting credits with ~10x token-cost reduction vs. dumping parsed HTML/markdown into the prompt (secondary source, not independently verified).
external_profiles.evaluation: First-party (train README): evaluated on a `miniv8` test set = 400 SimpleQA questions over 7,426 candidate tiles; fine-tuned model reaches peak QA score ≈ 0.785 vs ~0.715–0.730 for the untrained base Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B. Secondary reporting (VentureBeat / blogs, NOT verified in repo): tested across ~30M Wikipedia screenshot tiles, outperforms text-based RAG on six benchmarks, up to +18.1% accuracy. Metric is end-task QA accuracy (answer read by a VLM from retrieved tiles), i.e. retrieval quality measured through downstream answerability rather than pure nDCG/recall.
external_profiles.dependencies: Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B (base embedder) + published LoRA adapters Chrisyichuan/wiki-screenshot-embedding-lora; FAISS (index); FastAPI (serving); Playwright + Chrome CDP (rendering); poppler (PDF); Python 3.10+. Training env: torch==2.9.1+cu129, transformers==4.57.1; LoRA via `--lora-vit` (adapts both the LLM and the ViT vision encoder), ~25.4M trainable params (1.18% of 2.15B). Synthetic data pipeline uses Gemini (query generation + naturalness scoring), GPT-4o (self-containment filtering), and a VLM for false-negative removal. Repo layout: chromium/, render/, embed/, index/, serve/, train/ (separate uv project), plugin/ (Claude Code integration), demos/.

techniques.technique: Pixel-native tile retrieval (render-don't-parse)
techniques.what: Render each source doc to fixed-width screenshot tiles and embed the image directly with a VL embedder; the reader VLM answers from the pixel tile instead of parsed text.
techniques.value: For table/chart-heavy ATF docs this is the single biggest idea: a complex multi-row table that text/markdown parsing mangles stays a single intact retrievable image unit, and a vision reader reads cell values straight off it. Strong complement to (not replacement for) a text+graph lane — run it as a parallel visual retrieval lane for pages where parsing is lossy.

techniques.technique: Tile-by-visual-region instead of token-window chunking
techniques.what: Split long pages along visual/layout boundaries into tiles so a whole table or figure lands in one chunk, rather than cutting at arbitrary token counts.
techniques.value: Directly attacks the classic failure where a table gets split across two text chunks and the answer cell is orphaned — the exact problem your whole-table-retrieval work targets. Worth borrowing as a layout-aware chunk boundary heuristic even in a text pipeline.

techniques.technique: LoRA fine-tune of a VL embedder on in-domain screenshots (incl. --lora-vit on the ViT)
techniques.what: Adapt Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B with LoRA on ~115K domain screenshot/query pairs, tuning both the LLM and the vision tower; ~1.2% trainable params lifts QA from ~0.72 to ~0.785.
techniques.value: Shows a cheap, concrete recipe to specialize a retriever to a narrow visual domain (ATF forms, ballistic tables, schematics) without full fine-tune — a realistic path if generic embedders underperform on your document style.

techniques.technique: VLM-generated synthetic (query, positive-tile) pairs from your own corpus
techniques.what: Have a VLM (Gemini) read random tiles from the first 70% of each page and emit Q/A pairs, then reject layout-bound/unnatural questions.
techniques.value: A self-contained way to build training/eval data for a table-heavy corpus with no human labels — generate factoid questions whose answers live inside specific table cells/figures.

techniques.technique: Search-API hard-negative mining with VLM false-negative removal
techniques.what: For each (query, positive) pair, retrieve top-50 confusable tiles via the live search index, keep high-similarity ones (margin 0.95) as hard negatives, then run a VLM over each candidate to DELETE any negative that actually answers the query.
techniques.value: The false-negative-removal step is the gem: in ATF docs many near-duplicate tables/forms genuinely contain the answer, so naive hard negatives poison contrastive training. Auto-filtering them with a reader VLM gives a clean signal — adoptable for any retriever fine-tune, text or visual.

techniques.technique: Multi-stage LLM data-quality filtering (self-containment + naturalness scoring)
techniques.what: GPT-4o drops non-self-contained queries (~15%), Gemini scores naturalness and factoid-style-fit 1–5, keep only ≥4/≥4 — ~195K candidates → ~115K kept.
techniques.value: A reusable quality gate for any synthetic eval/training set you build for the ATF corpus, keeping questions answerable and realistic rather than artifact-driven.

techniques.technique: Answerability-based retrieval eval (QA score via a reader VLM)
techniques.what: Score retrieval by whether a VLM can read the correct answer off the retrieved tile(s) (miniv8: 400 SimpleQA Qs over 7,426 tiles → QA≈0.785), not by nDCG/recall alone.
techniques.value: For table QA, recall@k hides whether the retrieved unit actually contains the cell needed; an end-to-end answerability metric catches 'retrieved the right page, wrong fragment' failures your benchmark cares about.

techniques.technique: Image-as-query visual search
techniques.what: The same shared VL embedding space lets a cropped image (a chart, a form region) be the query, returning visually similar tiles.
techniques.value: Enables 'find documents that look like this form/table layout' lookups over an ATF corpus — useful for template/version matching that text queries can't express.

external_profiles.name: RAGFlow (infiniflow/ragflow)
external_profiles.summary: RAGFlow is a large, mature open-source RAG engine built around "deep document understanding": its DeepDoc parser uses vision models (OCR, layout recognition, table-structure recognition) to extract structured chunks from PDFs/DOCX/slides/scans, which feed a template-based chunking pipeline, a hybrid keyword+vector+rerank retriever, and optional GraphRAG and RAPTOR enhancement layers. As of ~v0.21–v0.26 it added an orchestrable ingestion pipeline (pluggable parsers MinerU/Docling, decoupled chunkers), agentic flows with MCP, and agent "memory". It is production-oriented (Docker, Elasticsearch or Infinity store, MinIO, Redis, MySQL) rather than a research library.
external_profiles.ingestion: DeepDoc is the core parser: a vision stack of OCR + layout recognition + table-structure recognition (TSR) that interprets complex PDF/DOCX/PPT/scanned/image layouts before chunking, rather than naive text extraction. Parser selection is a factory keyed on parser_id (naive, manual, table, paper, book, laws, presentation, etc.). v0.21 made ingestion an orchestrable pipeline with a redesigned, extensible Parser stage and pluggable external parsers MinerU and Docling. Async architecture: upload via API, tasks queued in Redis, background workers run parse→chunk→enhance→embed→index with 0.0–1.0 progress tracking. Built-in data connectors: Confluence, S3, Notion, Discord, Google Drive. A multimodal model can be invoked to interpret images embedded in PDF/DOCX.
external_profiles.chunking: "Template-based chunking" — multiple document-type templates (paper, book, laws, manual, presentation, table, Q&A, one, etc.) that segment according to the knowledge structure, marketed as intelligent + explainable with human-in-the-loop visual chunk editing (you can see and correct chunk boundaries in the UI). v0.21 decoupled the chunking step so users can plug in custom chunkers per knowledge structure. Each chunk is stored as a structured record with fields: content, tokenized content (content_ltks), page numbers, and associated image IDs; document title is prepended before embedding to preserve context.
external_profiles.retrieval: Hybrid by default: weighted keyword similarity + weighted vector cosine similarity (a fusion of sparse term-weighted matching over content_ltks and dense embeddings). When a rerank model is configured, the weighted vector-similarity term is replaced by a weighted reranking score (i.e. keyword + rerank). Described in the README as "multiple recall paired with fused re-ranking." AI-search mode uses keyword+vector hybrid; AI-chat can substitute rerank for the vector term. Optional retrieval-time enhancers configured per knowledge base: auto-keyword and auto-question expansion, plus knowledge-graph retrieval for multi-hop questions (iterative search across entity, relationship, and community-report chunks). Also supports a Tag knowledge base for tag-based filtering/recall.
external_profiles.graph: GraphRAG-inspired (also draws on mind-map). run_graphrag_for_kb() uses an LLM to extract entities + relationships into a knowledge graph; entity types are user-definable (organization, person, location, etc.). Key differentiator vs Microsoft GraphRAG: an explicit LLM-based entity-resolution/deduplication step merging synonyms (e.g. "2024" vs "Year 2024"). Produces node names, descriptions, and "communities" with community reports generated by the LLM at a chosen hierarchy level, used as global-search context. Verified limitation: in the documented version the graph is built per-document — it cannot link graphs across multiple documents due to memory/compute constraints. GraphRAG (and RAPTOR) execution was overhauled for batch execution / higher throughput. NOTE: I could NOT verify that RAGFlow uses Leiden community detection or LightRAG-style dual-level (low-level entity / high-level theme) keys — RAGFlow's own docs describe it as GraphRAG-inspired with communities + reports, not LightRAG dual-level; treat the LightRAG framing as a separate technique to consider, not something RAGFlow confirms it implements.
external_profiles.multimodal: DeepDoc's table-structure recognition extracts tables during parsing; there is a dedicated "table" parser template. Chunks carry associated image IDs so figures/page images are retrievable alongside text. A multimodal model can be enabled to "make sense of images within PDF or DOCX." Tables/charts/equations are handled inside the parsing layer rather than as a separately documented subsystem; I could not verify a dedicated equation-to-LaTeX or chart-data-extraction module beyond the general vision pipeline.
external_profiles.raptor: RAPTOR (Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval) runs as a post-parse preprocessing step: chunks are clustered by semantic similarity (not original order), each cluster summarized by the default chat model, recursively, building a tree where original chunks are leaves and summaries are higher nodes. Both original chunks and generated summaries get full-text + vector indexes. Params: Threshold (default 0.1, sim cutoff for grouping), Max cluster (default 64, max 1024), Max token per summary (default 256, max 2048). NOTE: docs do not confirm the specific clustering algorithm (the original RAPTOR paper uses UMAP + Gaussian Mixture Models, but RAGFlow's docs don't state UMAP/GMM — unverified).
external_profiles.agentic: Agentic workflow + MCP support (Aug 2025); a "converged context engine," pre-built agent templates, agent "Memory" (Dec 2025), and a Python/JavaScript code-executor component (May 2025) sandboxed via gVisor. Retrieval agent component can use the RAPTOR tree as default retrieval.
external_profiles.evaluation: No first-party evaluation/benchmark framework is documented in the README or core docs I checked. RAGFlow markets "grounded citations" / traceable chunks for human verification but does not ship a quantitative eval harness — unverified that one exists.
external_profiles.dependencies: Docker ≥24.0.0, Python ≥3.13. Document store: Elasticsearch OR Infinity (InfiniFlow's own hybrid vector+FTS DB). MinIO (object/blob store for files + page images), Redis (task queue), MySQL (metadata). gVisor (code-executor sandbox). Latest referenced image ~v0.26.1. techniques.technique: DeepDoc table-structure recognition (TSR)
techniques.what: Dedicated vision model that recognizes table cell grid/row/col spans from rendered PDF layout, plus a dedicated 'table' parser template, so a table becomes a structured object rather than mangled text.
techniques.value: Directly targets a table-heavy ATF corpus: reconstructs cell topology you can serialize to HTML/markdown and do cell-level QA over, instead of losing structure to naive text extraction.

techniques.technique: Title/context prepending before embedding
techniques.what: Document title (and structural context) is prepended to each chunk's text prior to encoding.
techniques.value: Cheap, high-ROI fix for table-row chunks that are meaningless without their table/section header — disambiguates near-identical rows across documents.

techniques.technique: Hybrid weighted keyword+vector with rerank substitution
techniques.what: Default fusion of weighted sparse term similarity (over tokenized content_ltks) and weighted dense cosine; when a reranker is present, rerank score replaces the vector term in the weighted sum.
techniques.value: A table/graph corpus has many exact-token signals (codes, part numbers, headers) where sparse recall beats pure dense; the explicit weight-and-swap scheme is a clean pattern to copy.

techniques.technique: LLM entity-resolution / dedup step in graph build
techniques.what: After entity extraction, an LLM merges synonymous entities ('2024' vs 'Year 2024') before the graph is finalized.
techniques.value: For a graph-based ATF RAG, this prevents node fragmentation that silently breaks multi-hop traversal — a concrete, adoptable step the original GraphRAG omits.

techniques.technique: Community detection + LLM community reports for global search
techniques.what: Graph nodes are grouped into communities; LLM writes a report per community at a chosen hierarchy level, used as global-query context.
techniques.value: Lets graph retrieval answer broad/aggregate questions ('summarize all X across the corpus') that node-level traversal can't, complementing local multi-hop.

techniques.technique: RAPTOR recursive summary tree indexed alongside leaves
techniques.what: Recursive semantic clustering + summarization builds a tree; both summaries and original chunks are indexed for full-text + vector search.
techniques.value: Gives long-context/aggregate answers over many tables (e.g. 'overall trend across all spec tables') while still allowing drill-down to exact rows.

techniques.technique: Auto-keyword and auto-question chunk enrichment
techniques.what: At ingest, keyword_extraction() and question_proposal() generate keywords and hypothetical questions stored with each chunk; gen_metadata() adds metadata.
techniques.value: HyDE-like query/keyword bridging boosts recall on terse table-cell chunks whose raw text shares few tokens with natural-language queries.

techniques.technique: Decoupled / pluggable chunker + parser stages
techniques.what: v0.21 split the ingestion pipeline so parsers (DeepDoc/MinerU/Docling) and chunkers are swappable per knowledge structure.
techniques.value: Architectural pattern: lets you route ATF doc types to specialized table-aware chunkers without forking the whole pipeline.

techniques.technique: Tag knowledge base + metadata-driven recall
techniques.what: Chunks can carry tags/metadata used as retrieval filters in addition to similarity.
techniques.value: Enables scoping retrieval to a document family / table type before ranking — useful when comparison questions must fan out to both sides of a known partition.

techniques.technique: Per-document graph scope (and its known limit)
techniques.what: RAGFlow builds the KG per document and explicitly does not link cross-document graphs (memory/compute).
techniques.value: A cautionary design point: if your ATF use case needs cross-document multi-hop, you must add the cross-doc entity-linking layer RAGFlow deliberately skips.

top_adopt.technique: LLM (or cluster+LLM-confirm) entity-resolution/dedup pass before community detection and PPR
top_adopt.benefit: Merges node variants (manufacturer aliases, FFL-holder spellings, '2024' vs 'Year 2024') that currently fragment the typed graph and silently break multi-hop traversal and community formation - directly improves relationship/pattern answer correctness on trafficking/trace questions.
top_adopt.risk: Over-merging distinct entities (two real people with same name) can create false multi-hop bridges; gate merges with a confidence threshold + type-match check and keep a merge audit log so GraphQualityAgent can flag suspicious merges.

top_adopt.technique: Title/section/document-header prepending before embedding table-row chunks
top_adopt.benefit: Near-identical table rows across years/editions/documents currently collide in vector space; prepending the table title + section + doc title disambiguates them so the right edition's row ranks first. Very high ROI for our cross-year ATF tables.
top_adopt.risk: Header text can dilute the row's own tokens and slightly hurt exact-match dense recall; keep the prepend short and ensure BM25/RowIndex still index the raw cell text un-prefixed.

top_adopt.technique: Answerability-based retrieval eval harness (reader model confirms the answer cell is in the retrieved unit)
top_adopt.benefit: Replaces recall@k blind spots that hide 'retrieved right page, wrong fragment' - the exact failure our whole-table-expansion and row-lookup work targets. Gives a real regression metric to tune lanes/boosts against.
top_adopt.risk: Reader-model judgments cost tokens and can be noisy; use a deterministic offline judge for CI reproducibility and reserve the LLM judge for periodic full runs.

top_adopt.technique: Parallel pixel/image retrieval lane for parse-lossy pages (render page->image->VLM reader)
top_adopt.benefit: For dense charts, scanned forms, and infographics where Docling/markdown is lossy, a vision reader reads values straight off the page image - closes our biggest remaining multimodal gap without replacing the text+graph lanes.
top_adopt.risk: Adds VLM inference cost/latency and a second index; scope it to pages flagged lossy by ParseQualityAgent (high empty/garble ratio or image-heavy) rather than the whole corpus to control cost.

top_adopt.technique: RAPTOR recursive summary tree over table/numeric chunks, indexed alongside leaves
top_adopt.benefit: Answers cross-table aggregate/trend questions ('overall trend across all spec or trace tables') that entity-centric Leiden community summaries cannot, while preserving drill-down to exact rows. Complements, not duplicates, our communities.
top_adopt.risk: Summary nodes can introduce un-grounded numbers; route any numeric claim sourced from a summary node back through GroundingVerifier against leaf chunks before generation.

top_adopt.technique: Delta-context window for VLM modal captioning (feed neighboring chunks when describing a table/figure)
top_adopt.benefit: Surrounding prose disambiguates cryptic ATF column headers and units when the VLM writes the [VLM CHART]/table caption, improving downstream entity extraction and retrievability of figure/table chunks.
top_adopt.risk: Larger captioning prompts cost more tokens and can let the VLM hallucinate from neighbor text; cap neighbor context to the immediately adjacent chunks and keep the caption extractive.

top_adopt.technique: VLM false-negative removal when building any retriever-tuning or eval negative set
top_adopt.benefit: ATF corpora are full of near-duplicate tables/forms that genuinely contain the answer; auto-deleting such 'hard negatives' with a reader model prevents poisoning any contrastive tuning or eval set we build.
top_adopt.risk: Only relevant once we build tuning/eval negatives; deferring is fine. Reader-model filtering adds cost and can mislabel borderline rows - sample-audit the deletions.

comparison.verdict_summary: OURS is already at or ahead of all three externals on the core ATF axes: layout/TSR parsing, deterministic exact table-row + SQL retrieval with cross-year consolidation, typed graph + Leiden communities + PPR, corrective/multi-hop/comparison retrieval, and grounding verification. The genuine gaps are not in raw capability but in graph hygiene, embedding disambiguation, evaluation rigor, and visual fallback. The highest-correctness-per-effort wins are small/medium: an explicit LLM entity-resolution pass (RAGFlow) to stop silent multi-hop breakage, header-prepending before embedding (RAGFlow) to separate near-identical cross-year rows, and an answerability-based eval harness (PixelRAG) to catch 'right page, wrong fragment' failures our row work is meant to fix. The one larger but defensible bet is a scoped pixel/VLM-reader lane (PixelRAG) for the minority of parse-lossy pages; skip domain LoRA, image-as-query, ingest-time HyDE, and store consolidation as low-ROI for this workload.
